title: Network Armor Terraform module: consolidated SG/NACL/private-dns/egress policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a composable Terraform module ("Network Armor") that bundles: security groups (least-privilege defaults + role-based templates), subnet-level NACL policy templates, private DNS forwarding and zone overrides, and a policy-driven egress controller (allow-lists, proxy integration, and per-environment exceptions). This module will be the standard IaC building block for Redwood Private VPC deployments and on-prem gateway stacks.

Motivation:
- We currently have duplicated, ad-hoc security controls across stacks which causes drift during upgrades and incidents.
- Customers deploying Private need a single, auditable Terraform module to enforce consistent perimeter controls and make upgrades predictable.
- Integrates with our rollout/fallback strategy for upgrades and enables automated health checks for network safety.

Goals:
1) Provide secure-by-default SG and NACL templates with clear variable-driven overrides.
2) Implement private DNS module capabilities: conditional forwarding to customer resolvers, internal zone registration for service discovery, and split-horizon support.
3) Egress policy engine: prioritized allow/deny rules, opt-in proxy chaining (egress-proxy module), and emergency cut-off switch.
4) Automated post-apply health checks and drift detection to validate config vs runtime (dns resolution tests, egress path probes, SG/NACL rule verify).
5) Migration and upgrade path for existing Private customers: state import helpers, automated plan diffs, and rollback guidance.

Design notes / decisions so far:
- Module will be broken into submodules (sg, nacl, dns, egress-checker) but published as a single registry module to make adoption easy.
- Use variable-driven role profiles (control-plane, runtime-host, infra-agent) to generate minimal SGs rather than a single monolithic SG that requires manual edits.
- Prefer explicit NACL allow lists per subnet tier with a default deny; where stateful apps require ephemeral ports, document recommended SG patterns instead of NACL open rules.
- Private DNS implemented with conditional aws_route53_resolver_rule resources and optional forwarding to customer inbound endpoints for hybrid setups.
- Egress policy uses a priority-ordered rule list with optional lambda-based policy evaluators for complex lookups (kept optional to avoid complexity).

API / Inputs (high level):
- var.environment (string)
- var.role_profile (string or list)
- var.allowed_egress_cidrs (list)
- var.egress_proxy_enabled (bool)
- var.proxy_endpoint (string)
- var.private_dns_forwarders (list)
- var.enable_drift_detection (bool)
- var.healthcheck_endpoints (map)

Outputs (high level):
- subnet_security_group_ids
- nacl_ids
- private_dns_associations
- egress_policy_id

Upgrade & migration plan:
- Provide a migration README and helper script: terraform import maps for common resource name mappings.
- A multi-step upgrade flow: 1) dry-run with special "preview" flag that simulates resource renames, 2) import-only mode to assert stateable resources, 3) apply with canary on a non-production VPC, 4) monitor health checks before full rollout.
- Backward compatibility: keep legacy variable names for one release with warning deprecation messages in module output.

Health checks & observability:
- Post-apply runbook: module will optionally trigger an AWS Lambda or GitHub Actions job that runs: DNS resolution tests for configured zones, TCP/HTTP probes to representative external endpoints via configured egress path, and rule enumeration to ensure applied SG/NACL matches the module plan.
- Export healthcheck logs to a central S3 bucket and a minimal CloudWatch metric (NetworkArmor.HealthCheck.Status) for Console dashboards.
- Emit a human-readable summary artifact (JSON) with failed checks and suggested rollbacks.

Testing strategy:
- Unit: terratest suites for each role_profile verifying generated SG rules and NACL behavior.
- Integration: ephemeral test VPC runs in CI (isolated account) that exercises DNS forwarding and egress proxy chaining.
- Chaos: simulate partial network failures and ensure emergency cut-off flips to deny-all without destroying infra.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module published in internal registry with versioned changelog and example repo.
- Automated health checks pass in CI for at least two reference configurations (customer-like and internal-only).
- Migration docs and state import mappings verified against 2 current customer setups.
- Security review completed and sign-off recorded.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module to internal registry and publish v0.1.0 (canary).
2) Deploy to staging Private stack used by Solutions Engineering.
3) Run health checks and manual validation by infra team.
4) Open a customer pilot cohort for 2 low-risk customers and perform guided upgrade.
5) Gradual ramp to general availability and tag deprecation windows for legacy patterns.

Artifacts & links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Network+Armor+Module
- Example repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-helm-examples/tree/network-armor
- Draft PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/428
- Healthcheck runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/network-healthchecks

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we require HSM/KMS integration for DNS secrets by default or make it opt-in? (security team preference needed)
- How strict should default egress allow-lists be for Managed customers vs self-hosted? Need PM decision on default posture.
- Tagging and naming convention alignment with existing terraform modules (ENG-34721 referenced) — current plan is to reuse "redwood:component" tags.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- (Marcus) Draft initial module scaffold and create registry entry (ETA 1 week).
- (Aisha) Schedule a security sync to resolve KMS and default posture questions.
- Create Terratest CI workflow and a staging apply job that runs automated health checks.

Notes on follow-ups and tracking:
- Add a small follow-up ticket for Lighthouse/Console dashboard integration to show NetworkArmor health metrics and recent failures.
- Track any breaking changes to naming in a migration-mapping document inside the repo.
